title: Single-coordinate replacement bound
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $F$ be a multilinear polynomial on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ with degree at most $k$, and fix a coordinate $i$. Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are mutually independent random variables on this space, and likewise $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ are mutually independent. Let $0<\rho<1$, and assume every $X_j$ and $Y_j$ is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive, has mean zero, and has second moment one. Suppose also that $X_j=Y_j$ for every $j\ne i$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is three times continuously differentiable and $|\psi'''(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$, where $C\ge0$, then
\[\left|\mathbb E\bigl[\psi(F(X))\bigr]-\mathbb E\bigl[\psi(F(Y))\bigr]\right|\le \frac{C}{3}\left(\frac1\rho\right)^{3k}\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^{3/2},\]
where $F(X)$ and $F(Y)$ denote the polynomial evaluated on the respective random inputs, and $\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]$ is the influence of the restriction of $F$ to Boolean sign inputs.
hypotheses_covered: Each $X_j$ and $Y_j$ has second moment one
caveat: The formal statement defines influence by applying the Boolean-cube influence formula to the Walsh-basis evaluation of the coefficient family; the phrase “restriction of $F$ to Boolean sign inputs” is intended to describe that specific function.
